# Related work {#sec-related}

**Planning in language models.** Hidden states anticipate tokens several positions
ahead [@pal2023futurelens; @wu2024plan; @men2024lookahead]. Attribution graphs expose
explicit planning in rhyming and in article choice [@lindsey2025biology;
@ameisen2025attribution]. @hanna2026latent show that such planning emerges with
scale in Qwen3 and identify the circuit that retrieves the rhyme plan near the end of
line 2. Three studies locate the plan at the line boundary or probe it there
[@maar2026plan; @ma2026plan; @jacopin2026improvisation]. These works ask whether and
where a plan exists and whether it can be steered. We ask which path it takes to its
target, and show that the published accounts measure different lookup sites whose
proportions change with scale (@sec-storage).

**Causal mediation and patching.** Route accounting builds on activation patching
and causal mediation [@vig2020mediation; @meng2022rome; @geiger2025abstraction;
@chan2022scrubbing] and follows their best practices for metrics and corruption
[@zhang2024patching; @heimersheim2024patching]. It is closest to path patching
[@wang2023ioi; @goldowskydill2023path] and to attention knockout on information flow
[@geva2023recall]. It differs in three ways. The paths are defined over positions
rather than components. Emission through generated text is separated from
persistence. And sufficiency and necessity are reported side by side with an explicit
interaction term, which matters where storage is redundant (@sec-storage). @mueller2026mediator
argue for evaluating mechanisms against explicit causal mediators; our mediators are
positions and generated tokens.

**Anchors, separators and registers.** Structural tokens aggregate information:
label words in in-context learning [@wang2023labelwords], separators that summarize
a segment [@chen2024sepllm], attention sinks [@xiao2024sinks], and register tokens in
vision transformers [@darcet2024registers]. @shih2026registers study whether models
read the registers they write in scratchpads. The line-end copy and the stored hidden
pick extend this picture. Under causal tests, these positions store task content
that a later position reads directly, and the line-end copy grows with scale and
distance.

**Chain-of-thought faithfulness and monitoring.** Written reasoning can be
unfaithful to the computation behind an answer [@turpin2023unfaithful;
@lanham2023faithfulness; @chen2025reasoning]. Models can compute with filler tokens
[@pfau2024dots] and could in principle encode reasoning steganographically
[@roger2023steganography]. Monitoring the chain of thought is valuable but fragile
[@korbak2025monitorability; @baker2025monitoring]. It is more robust when reasoning
is necessary for the task [@emmons2025cot]. These studies measure behaviour. Route
accounting measures the internal paths directly. Its two findings bear on
monitorability: written values are used in proportion to their leverage, and
unwritten content is looked up at a few prompt positions rather than passed along
the generated text by early relay. Work on eliciting secrets from models trained to keep them
[@cywinski2025taboo] studies hidden content that training installs. Our hidden choice
arises without any training.

**Architectures.** Gated DeltaNet and related recurrent layers replace attention
with a fixed-size state [@yang2025gateddeltanet]. Hybrids interleave them with
attention [@qwen2026qwen35], and sliding-window hybrids limit how far most layers can
see [@beltagy2020longformer; @gemma3]. These designs restrict direct lookup, which is
why we use them as stress tests. In both, the models keep the lookup where some layer
can still perform it (@sec-stress).
